# One-way random-effects models

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Introduction to Random Effects and Mixed Models*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-05-25.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/Lecture15RandomEffectsMixedModels.pdf))
covers fixed versus random effects,
one-way random-effects ANOVA,
variance components and their method-of-moments estimates,
and nested random effects
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

# Multilevel models: complete, no, and partial pooling

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Multilevel Models*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-05-27.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/Lecture16MultilevelModels.pdf))
covers complete, no, and partial pooling of the Minnesota radon data,
random intercepts and slopes with `lmer()`,
and shrinkage
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

{{< include _subfiles/intro-multilevel-models/_sec-pooling.qmd >}}

# Adding predictors to a multilevel model

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Multilevel Models II*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-06-01.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/Lecture17MultilevelModelsII.pdf))
covers adding county-level uranium as a group-level predictor for the radon data,
and multilevel logistic regression with `glmer()`
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::
